*** SPRINT 75 / V0.29.30 IS UNDER WAY. US-560 CLOSED passes:false -- ITS PREMISE IS REFUTED BY THE HARDWARE, not by a defect. BL-034 filed, needs an ATLAS RULING (CIO ratify). THE SPRINT IS NOT BLOCKED: US-561 is explicitly resolution-independent and 563/564/565/566 are unrelated, so the next iteration should pick up US-561. 1 of 11 stories closed, 0 passing. ***

*** FIRST, THE ENVIRONMENTAL CORRECTION THAT UNBLOCKED THE STORY: THE PI IS REACHABLE FROM THIS HARNESS. `ssh chi-eclipse-01` works with BatchMode and no password. The Sprint 74 handoff said the Pi was unreachable and listed every Pi read as "hardware, not closable on the dev box" -- that claim was STALE and it cost Sprint 74 a deferral. One ssh settled it in seconds and turned a deferred story into a finding. RE-TEST AN ENVIRONMENTAL CLAIM BEFORE INHERITING IT. The deploy tree on the Pi is /home/mcornelison/Projects/Eclipse-01 (found via `systemctl show eclipse-obd -p WorkingDirectory`, NOT ~/OBD2v2). Several of the "STILL OWED" Pi reads in the old note are probably closable now. ***

WHAT US-560 ASKED AND WHAT HAPPENED: apply the US-552 mode pin to the live Pi and verify fb0 reads 480,320. I re-confirmed the premise (fb0 = 1280,720), discovered the connector from sysfs (HDMI-A-1 connected / HDMI-A-2 disconnected -- exactly one, so interlock 2 passes), and RAN deploy/set-display-mode.sh on the Pi. IT REFUSED AT INTERLOCK 5 AND WROTE NOTHING. The panel does not advertise 480x320. EDID: mfg=OSY, model=HDMI35, PREFERRED detailed timing 1280x720; advertised list is 1280x720 / 1920x1080 / 1280x1024 / 1440x900 / 1280x800 / 1024x768 / 800x600 / 720x480 / 640x480 / 720x400. No 480x320 anywhere. THERE IS NOTHING TO PIN.

NOT A SCRIPT BUG -- tests/deploy/test_set_display_mode.py 9 passed / 0 failed. The script did exactly what it was built for, and its own refusal text says "that is an EDID finding for Atlas (US-552) -- not something to force here." BL-034 is that finding.

*** ROOT CAUSE OF THE FALSE PREMISE IS A FABRICATED TEST FIXTURE, AND THIS IS THE LESSON WORTH CARRYING: US-552's bash catalog carried `# The panel's advertised mode list as a 3.5" 480x320 HDMI panel reports it: PANEL_MODES='1920x1080 1280x720 640x480 480x320'`. Nobody had read the panel's EDID. The fixture ASSERTED a hardware fact, which made its own suite UNFALSIFIABLE -- US-552 could never have gone red on the real panel, because the fixture guaranteed the happy path existed. Same shape as the latched magnetometer and IAT-as-ambient: a value standing in for a measurement nobody took. GENERALISE: WHEN A FIXTURE STANDS IN FOR HARDWARE NOBODY HAS READ, LABEL IT SYNTHETIC AND SAY WHAT IT EXERCISES. The moment a fixture comment says "as the panel reports it", it has become a measurement that was never taken. ***

SECONDARY CAUSE, A UNIT CONFLATION: US-552 correctly refused to ground its 480x320 default against a second copy of the literal, and grounded it against docs/hardware-reference.md instead -- but that row ("Resolution | 480 x 320 pixels") is the GLASS, and the script consumes it as a KMS SIGNAL TIMING. Right discipline, wrong quantity. The OSOYOO HDMI35 is a SCALER panel: 480x320 glass behind a chip that accepts standard HDMI timings and downsamples in hardware. A native KMS mode was never on offer. GROUND A CONSTANT AGAINST THE DOC *AND CHECK THE DOC MEANS THE SAME QUANTITY* -- pin the UNIT, not just the source.

WHAT I CHANGED (TEST-ONLY, AND DELIBERATELY DISPOSITION-INDEPENDENT -- the target mode is Atlas's call and I did not pre-empt it; nothing in deploy/ or src/): relabelled PANEL_MODES as the SYNTHETIC write-path fixture it actually is; added OSOYOO_HDMI35_MEASURED_MODES carrying the command and date it was measured; added SCENARIO 15 pinning that the REAL panel makes the script refuse with the boot cmdline untouched (6 assertions; catalog 50 -> 56). Scenario 15 encodes NO ruling on what to pin instead, so it stays valid whichever way BL-034 goes. A blocker rots; a test does not.

*** THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PIN: the Pi is not "failing to reach native" -- there IS no native mode, and the panel has been hardware-downscaling all along. A 34px driver-must-read value lands on the 320px glass at roughly 13-15 physical px (0.444 if the panel stretches 16:9, 0.375 if it letterboxes -- I measured the SIGNAL, not the glass, so both are given). That is about HALF the F-127 floor and is a better explanation of the marginal arm's-length reads than anything in F-132. US-560's own AC-5 was right to be suspicious of the scale. ***

BL-034 RECOMMENDATION (Atlas rules, CIO ratifies -- DO NOT FORCE): pin 720x480. It is the ONLY advertised mode matching the glass's 3:2 aspect (480/320 = 720/480 = 1.5), so the scale is a uniform 0.667 with zero aspect distortion, and a 34px value lands at ~23px -- ~1.5-1.8x better than today. It needs NO code change and NO forcing: `ECLIPSE_DISPLAY_MODE=720x480 sudo bash deploy/set-display-mode.sh` passes interlock 3 on its own terms. FORCING 480x320 with a D-suffix modeline bypasses EDID validation and can scan out BLACK in a car with no local recovery -- that is exactly what interlock 3 exists to stop, and guessing a plausible value in an unmeasured subsystem is how the last three fabrications happened.

*** SECOND FINDING -- PM MUST READ THIS BEFORE US-555/556/557 RUN. The chromium kiosk (eclipse-dashboard.service, NOT "eclipse-kiosk") runs with NO --window-size and NO --force-device-scale-factor, so it fills the X screen and the dashboard renders into a 1280x720 CSS-PIXEL VIEWPORT. But US-557's band budget ("body 224px; 3 rows + footer = 222") is ~320-canvas arithmetic. THE LAYOUT IS BUDGETED AGAINST ONE CANVAS AND RENDERED ON ANOTHER -- the exact value-changed-here / measurement-left-behind shape US-555's own conditionalOutcome warns about. If the three chrome stories are built and IN-CAR-validated at 1280x720, settling BL-034 afterwards silently invalidates all three. I am FLAGGING, NOT RULING: I measured the ABSENCE of any overriding flag, not the in-browser viewport. Someone should measure the actual viewport before the chrome stories run. ***

KNOCK-ON FOR F-133 / THE FREEZE: Atlas ordered US-560 first because every freeze observation to date is at 720p/1080p and "the shipping configuration has never been tested". It turns out 720p IS THE SHIPPING CONFIGURATION -- the panel asks for it. So the freeze was never observed at the wrong resolution, and the mode pin is NOT the untested lever it was believed to be. "Re-measure the freeze after the mode pin lands" needs re-thinking on that basis. F-127's in-car legibility gate also stays OPEN: US-560 was to discharge it "once the read is taken at native res", and there is no native res, so the gate needs re-specifying against whatever BL-034 rules.

FOR PM: US-552 is marked passes:true in the Sprint 74 archive. Its CODE is sound and its interlocks did their job today. Its ACCEPTANCE rested on a fixture that asserted hardware nobody had read. Whether that warrants a note on the record is PM's call, not mine.

ENVIRONMENT (carried forward + corrected): `make` is NOT on PATH -- exits 127, WHICH READS LIKE A PASS; use `python -m ruff check <file>`. `mypy` is NOT installed. **COMPOUND BASH IS REFUSED -- both `a; b` and `a && b` came back as "contains multiple operations"; run ONE command per Bash call.** `/tmp` is NOT writable -- scratch files go INSIDE the repo and must be rm'd before committing. `pytest -q` prints NO summary line on this tree: redirect to a file, then read the tail AND `grep -cE '^(FAILED|ERROR)'`. **NEW, PI-SIDE: `xxd` and `edid-decode` are NOT installed on the Pi, but `python3` is -- parse /sys/class/drm/<connector>/edid with a python3 one-liner rather than assuming a tool exists.** **NEW: the Pi's deploy tree is /home/mcornelison/Projects/Eclipse-01.** The index lock was CLEAR all session; the commit went through normally.
